messages.subject: Responses to my posting of 26March: Covariate increases AIC (+2)
parts:
Hello everyone
I received four responses to the problem I posted on 26 March, which relate=
d to variances in Point Transects (https://www.jiscmail.ac.uk/cgi-bin/webad=
min?A2=3Dind1203&L=3DDISTANCE-SAMPLING&F=3D&S=3D&P=3D6125


1. From Eric Rexstad: there is a known bug that underestimates the enc=
ounter rate variance in point transects. This problem will be corrected in =
Distance 6.1, and a beta version is available to fix it now also. Details a=
re below. I downloaded the beta release and it increased all my variances b=
ut did not correct the mysterious increase in precision that I observed aft=
er adding a covariate which didn't appear to improve the model at all.


2. From Len Thomas: there may be an additional problem with MCDS varia=
nce estimation; he is looking into this further.


3. Falk Huettman also sent some interesting references about alternati=
ve statistical modelling approaches, as follows:

Whittingham, MJ; Stephens, PA; Bradbury, RB; Freckleton, RP. 2006. Why do w=
e still use stepwise modelling in ecology and behaviour? JOURNAL OF ANIMAL =
ECOLOGY 75: 1182-1189

Breiman, L. 2001. Statistical modeling: The two cultures. STATISTICAL SCIEN=
CE 16: 287-294

Oppel S, Strobl C, Huettmann F. 2009. Alternative methods to quantify varia=
ble importance in ecology. Technical Report Number 65, Department of Statis=
tics, University of Munich http://www.stat.uni-muenchen.de



4. David Lawrence Miller reported that standardising the covariate (su=
btracting the mean and dividing by the SE) had resolved a similar problem w=
ith MRDS - but this didn't help in my case (MCDS).


Past correspondence about the known bug follow. Many thanks to Eric, Len, F=
alk, and Dave for their ideas and assistance.
Deb Wilson

From: Eric Rexstad [mailto:er...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk]

To: Deb Wilson
Cc: Len Thomas
Subject: Fwd: Re: [DIST-SAMP] Bug in DISTANCE 6.0: Estimation of encounter =
rate variance
Deb:

Problems with the encounter rate variance estimates in Distance 6.0 are res=
tricted to point transect data only (as described by Rachel Fewster in this=
email).

-------- Original Message --------
Subject: Re: [DIST-SAMP] Bug in DISTANCE 6.0: Estimation of encou=
nter rate variance
Date: Wed, 13 Apr 2011 15:13:47 +1200
From: Rachel Fewster <r.fe...@auckland.ac.nz>
Reply-To: Rachel Fewster <r.fe...@auckland.ac.nz>
To: DISTANCE...@jiscmail.ac.uk
Dear all,
Just to clarify Len's typo below, as I understand it the bug was
entirely with estimator P2 for point transects, not with R2 for line
transects.
Thanks Tim for drawing this to everyone's attention.
Rachel Fewster

On Wed, 13 Apr 2011, Distance Development wrote:
> > List,
> >
> > Further to Tim Ritter's report of a problem with CDS point transect varia=
nce
> > estimation, we have confirmed that this is a Bug with the R2 estimator, h=
ave
> > fixed it, and will be issuing a new release of Distance shortly.
> >
> > The bug report is here:
> > http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=3D92
> > More details (from the bug report response) is given below.
> >
> > - Len Thomas
> >
> > From
> > http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=3D92
> >
> > The problem was that for estimator P2, a routine was returning the varian=
ce of
> > the estimated encounter rate, when it should have been the standard error=
--
> > i.e., a square root was not being taken.
> >
> > Typically the standard error on encounter rate will be less than 1, and h=
ence
> > the variance is smaller than the SE, and hence using variance instead of
> > standard error has caused Distance to report a SE and CV that is smaller =
than it
> > should be.
> >
> > We will issue a new release of Distance shortly. Since P2 is the default
> > estimator of encounter rate variance, we recommend that CDS and MCDS poin=
t
> > transect analyses that were run in Distance 6.0 Release 1 and 2 be re-run=
in
> > the new release to check the analytic variance estimator.
> >
> > We apologize for any problems caused by this bug.
> >
